rationale: Luke 17:3-4 sets side by side two sayings that Matthew 18 separates by five verses: "If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him" and "Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, 'I repent,' you must forgive him" (BSB). Matthew has "If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately" (18:15) and Peter's "Up to seven times?" answered with "seventy-seven times" (18:21-22). The NABRE notes say that "Mt 18:21–22 correspond to Lk 17:4." The wording differs: Luke's verb for rebuking is ἐπιτίμησον where Matthew has ἔλεγξον, Luke has no witnesses and no church, Luke's seven is "in a day," and Luke names repentance as the condition. The editions split on "against you" in both Gospels. In Luke 17:3 the Byzantine, Greek Orthodox and both Textus Receptus texts read εἰς σὲ and the SBL, Nestle, Westcott-Hort and Tischendorf texts do not; at Matthew 18:15 the split is the same except that the SBL text includes the words. A synoptic parallel of sayings is parallel/strong under this curriculum's rule (conn-matt16-sign-mark8), not explicit. Poole judged that Luke's saying "seemeth to have been spoken at another time, and upon some other occasion"; the row grades the shared sayings, not whether they were spoken once.
